entities.summary: The red thread of fate, also referred to as the red thread of marriage, the invisible string theory and other variants, is a Chinese belief originating from Taoism. It is commonly thought of as an invisible red cord around the finger of those that are destined to meet one another in a certain situation, as they are "their one true love". The Taoist deity in charge of "the red thread" is Yuè Xià Lǎorén (月下老人), often abbreviated to Yuè Lǎo (月老), the old lunar matchmaker god, who is in charge of marriages. Red String of Fate is a legend. Classified as Tier E (Oral Tradition) evidence. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Red String of Fate has had a significant impact on Chinese culture and marriage traditions, with many couples believing that their union is predestined. This legend has been passed down for centuries, influencing the way people approach relationships and marriage.
